{{Top|leg}}
[[File:JangoFettKeldabeKiss-OpenSeasons3.jpg|thumb|right|350px|Jango Fett performing a violent ''kov'nyn'' on a Jedi on [[Galidraan/Legends|Galidraan]]]]
{{Quote|And what's a ''kov'nyn?"<br />"''A head-butt. A Keldabe kiss.|Etain Tur-Mukan and Ordo Skirata|<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>}}
"'''Keldabe kiss'''", or "'''''mirshmure'cya'''''" in [[Mando'a/Legends|Mando'a]], was a [[List of phrases and slang/Legends|slang]] term for a '''''kov'nyn''''', a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] headbutt. Performed with a [[Armor/Legends|helmet]], a ''kov'nyn'' could either be employed to cause injury to an opponent in [[Unarmed combat/Legends|unarmed combat]], or in a gentler capacity between two Mandalorians as an [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|armored]] greeting, contributing to the "[[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]] kiss" nickname.

==Description==
''Kov'nyn'' was the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] term for a headbutt, performed while wearing a [[Armor/Legends|helmet]].<ref name="O66" /> The term came from the Mandalorian [[Language/Legends|language]] of [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']], where it was derived from the words ''kovid'' and ''nynir'', meaning "head" and "strike", respectively.<ref name="Mando'a">{{WebCite|url=http://www.karentraviss.com/page20/page26/index.html|text=Mando'a|author=Karen Traviss|work=[http://www.karentraviss.com Karen Traviss]|archivedate=20110925083955}}</ref> A ''kov'nyn'' was a Mandalorian [[Unarmed combat/Legends|unarmed combat]] technique,<ref name="O66" /> utilizing the protection [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|their armor]] afforded them in an offensive manner.<ref name="Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>

Over [[Time/Legends|time]], a gentle headbutt consisting of a tapping of helmets together at the forehead, came to be a stand-in gesture for a kiss among Mandalorians adorned in full armor. The practice led to the development of the [[List of phrases and slang/Legends|slang]] term "[[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]] kiss," derived from the name of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore's]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]].<ref name="O66" />

==History==
{{Quote|He knew what it was to be a kid waiting to die, so I reckon he'd have given the aiwha-bait a good hard ''kov'nyn'' and sent him on his way.|Kal Skirata, assuring his adopted son Ordo that Jango Fett would have kept him safe from the Kaminoans had he not been there|<ref name="O66" />}}
By the final [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the term "Keldabe kiss" had become a recognized slang term for a Mandalorian headbutt. Because a gentle headbutt was used by Mandalorian couples in lieu of a typical kiss when they were wearing full armor and a helmet, a number of non-Mandalorians who had seen the gesture and yet were unfamiliar with its origin came to believe that an armored headbutt was a typical Mandalorian greeting.<ref name="O66" />

[[File:JangoHeadbutt.jpg|thumb|left|350px|Jango Fett striking Obi-Wan Kenobi with a ''kov'nyn'' on Kamino]]
In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]],<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> the Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] and reigning [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]]<ref name="O66" /> performed a violent ''kov'nyn'' on a [[Unidentified Jedi (Myles' killer)|Jedi]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Galidraan/Legends|Galidraan]], during a devastating [[Battle of Galidraan|battle]] between a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] taskforce and the [[True Mandalorians]].<ref name="OpenSeasons3">[[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 3|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 3]]</ref> Twenty years later, in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Fett performed another armored headbutt on the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], during [[Mission to Kamino (Separatist Crisis)/Legends|their fight]] on the [[Water/Legends|watery]] world of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].<ref name="AotC">{{Film|II}}</ref>

Near the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]—a [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-spanning conflict between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]—in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the former [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commando]]-turned-Mandalorian [[Fi Skirata]], was waiting in the marketplace of the Mandalore town [[Enceri]] for the arrival of his girlfriend, [[Parja Bralor]]. When Bralor arrived, she fondly greeted Skirata with a true "Keldabe kiss," affectionately tapping the forehead of her helmet to his by way of hello.<ref name="O66" />

During the tumultuous build up to the [[Second Galactic Civil War]] in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[President/Legends|President]] [[Thrackan Sal-Solo]] put out a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on the [[Solo family/Legends|family]] of his hated cousin, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]. Seeking to protect his family, Solo traveled to [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] where he allied himself with his former foe [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]—on world at Sal-Solo's request for Mandalorian military aid—who outfitted Solo with a suit of all-concealing Mandalorian armor and had the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] masquerade as a Mandalorian subordinate of his. Once Solo was close to his cousin, he attacked and headbutted him with the borrowed Mandalorian helmet, before Fett's granddaughter [[Mirta Gev]] finally [[Blaster/Legends|shot]] and [[Death/Legends|killed]] Sal-Solo.<ref name="Bloodlines">''[[Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The terms "Keldabe kiss" and "''kov'nyn''" were first introduced to ''[[Star Wars]]'' continuity in the [[Republic Commando|''Republic Commando'' novel]] [[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel|''Order 66'']], written by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]] and published [[September 16]], [[2008]]. The action of a Mandalorian headbutt first appeared in the second ''Star Wars'' [[Prequel trilogy|prequel]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], [[Retroactive continuity|retroactively]] making the [[2002]] film the first appearance of the act, itself.
